99:   if (a?.format) fragments.push(`format: ${a.format}`);
100:   const trimmed = draftText.trim().slice(0, 280);
101:   if (trimmed) fragments.push(trimmed);
102:   return fragments.join(" · ").trim();
103: }
104: 
105: /** Hash a query to dedupe. */
106: function hashQuery(q: string): string {
107:   // Cheap FNV-1a — we don't need crypto, just stable identity.
108:   let h = 0x811c9dc5;
109:   for (let i = 0; i < q.length; i++) {
110:     h ^= q.charCodeAt(i);
111:     h = Math.imul(h, 0x01000193);
112:   }
113:   return (h >>> 0).toString(36);
114: }
115: 
116: function sameAsRecent(q: string): boolean {
117:   return (
118:     hashQuery(q) === hashQuery(state.lastQuery) &&
119:     Date.now() - state.lastQueryAt < QUERY_CACHE_TTL_MS
120:   );
121: }
122: 
123: /** Stop any pending or running work. */
124: export function stopBackgroundResearch(): void {
125:   if (debounceTimer) {
126:     clearTimeout(debounceTimer);
127:     debounceTimer = null;
128:   }
129:   setStatus("idle");
130: }
131: 
132: /** Configure the research watcher. Safe to call repeatedly — the latest
133:  *  args win. */
134: export function startBackgroundResearch(args: {
135:   client: ConvexClient | null;
136:   brief: ProjectBrief | null;
137:   folioId: string | null;
138: }): void {
139:   activeClient = args.client;
140:   activeBrief = args.brief;
141:   activeFolioId = args.folioId;
142:   // No client = no remote research; mark idle but still emit a tick so
143:   // the UI knows we're listening.
144:   setStatus(activeClient ? "idle" : "idle");
145: }
146: 
147: /** Re-run research now (used on folio switch and on initial load). */
148: export function kickBackgroundResearch(draftText: string): void {
149:   if (!activeFolioId) return;
150:   schedule(draftText, 0);
151: }
152: 
153: /** Notify the watcher that the draft has changed. Debounced. */
154: export function onDraftChanged(draftText: string): void {
155:   if (!activeFolioId) return;
156:   schedule(draftText, DEBOUNCE_MS);
157: }
158: 
159: function schedule(draftText: string, delay: number): void {
160:   if (debounceTimer) clearTimeout(debounceTimer);
161:   debounceTimer = setTimeout(() => {
162:     debounceTimer = null;
163:     void runOnce(draftText);
164:   }, delay);
165: }
166: 
167: async function runOnce(draftText: string): Promise<void> {
168:   if (!activeClient || !activeFolioId) return;
169:   const query = deriveQuery(activeBrief, draftText);
170:   if (!query || query.length < 20) return; // too thin to be useful
171:   if (sameAsRecent(query)) return;
172: 
173:   state.lastQuery = query;
174:   state.lastQueryAt = Date.now();
175:   setStatus("running");
176:   notify();
177: 
178:   try {
179:     const context = activeBrief
180:       ? `${activeBrief.answers.audience ?? ""} · ${activeBrief.answers.goal ?? ""}`.trim()
181:       : undefined;
182:     const apparatusSettings = await loadApparatusSettingsFromIdb();
183:     const configured = await searchWithConfiguredProvider(
184:       query,
185:       context,
186:       apparatusSettings,
187:     );
188:     const res =
189:       configured ??
190:       ((activeClient
191:         ? await activeClient.action(api.research.searchSources, {
192:             query,
193:             context,
194:           })
195:         : { results: [], provider: "offline" }) as {
196:         results: Source[];
197:         provider: string;
198:       });
199:     state.lastProvider = res.provider;
200:     setStatus("saving");
201:     await persist(res.results ?? [], query);
202:     setStatus("idle");
203:   } catch (err) {
204:     setStatus("error", (err as Error).message);
205:   }
206: }
207: 
208: const TINYFISH_SEARCH_URL = "https://api.search.tinyfish.ai/v1/search";
209: 
210: async function searchWithConfiguredProvider(
211:   query: string,
212:   context: string | undefined,
213:   settings: ApparatusSettings,
214: ): Promise<{ results: Source[]; provider: string } | null> {
215:   switch (settings.researchProvider) {
216:     case "tinyfish":
217:       return searchTinyFishInBrowser(query, context, settings);
218:     case "model-web-search":
219:       return searchModelEndpoint(query, context, settings);
220:     case "web-mcp":
221:       return searchWebMcp(query, context, settings);
222:     case "hosted":
223:     default:
224:       return null;
225:   }
226: }
227: 
228: async function searchTinyFishInBrowser(
229:   query: string,
230:   context: string | undefined,
231:   settings: ApparatusSettings,
232: ): Promise<{ results: Source[]; provider: string } | null> {
233:   const key = settings.tinyFishApiKey.trim();
234:   if (!key) return null;
235:   try {
236:     const res = await fetch(TINYFISH_SEARCH_URL, {
237:       method: "POST",
238:       headers: {
239:         "content-type": "application/json",
240:         authorization: `Bearer ${key}`,
241:       },
242:       body: JSON.stringify({
243:         query,
244:         context: context ?? "",
245:         num_results: settings.tinyFishMaxResults,
246:       }),
247:     });
248:     if (!res.ok) return null;
249:     const data = (await res.json()) as { results?: unknown };
250:     const results = normalizeSources(data.results, settings.tinyFishMaxResults);
251:     return results.length ? { results, provider: "tinyfish:byok" } : null;
252:   } catch {
253:     return null;
254:   }
255: }
256: 
257: async function searchModelEndpoint(
258:   query: string,
259:   context: string | undefined,
260:   settings: ApparatusSettings,
261: ): Promise<{ results: Source[]; provider: string } | null> {
262:   const aiSettings = await loadAiSettingsFromIdb();
263:   if (!aiSettings) return null;
264:   return runClientResearchWebSearch(
265:     {
266:       query,
267:       context,
268:       maxResults: settings.tinyFishMaxResults,
269:       instructions:
270:         "If the selected provider exposes a web-search tool or model-native search mode, use it before answering.",
271:     },
272:     aiSettings,
273:   );
274: }
275: 
276: async function searchWebMcp(
277:   query: string,
278:   context: string | undefined,
279:   settings: ApparatusSettings,
280: ): Promise<{ results: Source[]; provider: string } | null> {
281:   const endpoint = settings.mcpEndpointUrl.trim();
282:   const toolName = settings.mcpToolName.trim() || "search";
283:   if (!endpoint) return null;
284:   try {
285:     const headers: Record<string, string> = {
286:       "content-type": "application/json",
287:     };
288:     const token = settings.mcpBearerToken.trim();
289:     if (token) headers.authorization = `Bearer ${token}`;
290:     const res = await fetch(endpoint, {
291:       method: "POST",
292:       headers,
293:       body: JSON.stringify({
294:         jsonrpc: "2.0",
295:         id: `twyne-${Date.now()}`,
296:         method: "tools/call",
297:         params: {
298:           name: toolName,
299:           arguments: {
300:             query,
301:             context,
302:             max_results: settings.tinyFishMaxResults,
303:           },
304:         },
305:       }),
306:     });
307:     if (!res.ok) return null;
308:     const data = await res.json();
309:     const results = normalizeMcpSources(data, settings.tinyFishMaxResults);
310:     return results.length ? { results, provider: `mcp:${toolName}` } : null;
311:   } catch {
312:     return null;
313:   }
314: }
315: 
316: function normalizeMcpSources(value: unknown, maxResults: number): Source[] {
317:   const direct = normalizeSources(value, maxResults);
318:   if (direct.length) return direct;
319:   if (!value || typeof value !== "object") return [];
320:   const rec = value as Record<string, unknown>;
321:   for (const key of ["results", "sources", "data"]) {
322:     const fromKey = normalizeSources(rec[key], maxResults);
323:     if (fromKey.length) return fromKey;
324:   }
325:   const result = rec.result;
326:   if (result && typeof result === "object") {
327:     const fromResult = normalizeMcpSources(result, maxResults);
328:     if (fromResult.length) return fromResult;
329:     const content = (result as Record<string, unknown>).content;
330:     if (Array.isArray(content)) {
331:       for (const item of content) {
332:         if (!item || typeof item !== "object") continue;
333:         const text = (item as Record<string, unknown>).text;
334:         if (typeof text !== "string") continue;
335:         try {
336:           const parsed = JSON.parse(text);
337:           const fromText = normalizeMcpSources(parsed, maxResults);
338:           if (fromText.length) return fromText;
339:         } catch {
340:           // Ignore non-JSON text content.
341:         }
342:       }
343:     }
344:   }
345:   return [];
346: }
347: 
348: function normalizeSources(value: unknown, maxResults: number): Source[] {
349:   if (!Array.isArray(value)) return [];
350:   return value
351:     .map((item) => {
352:       if (!item || typeof item !== "object") return null;
353:       const rec = item as Record<string, unknown>;
354:       const url = typeof rec.url === "string" ? rec.url.trim() : "";
355:       if (!/^https?:\/\//i.test(url)) return null;
356:       const title = typeof rec.title === "string" ? rec.title.trim() : "";
357:       const source: Source = {
358:         title: title || url,
359:         url,
360:         snippet:
361:           typeof rec.snippet === "string" && rec.snippet.trim()
362:             ? rec.snippet.trim()
363:             : typeof rec.summary === "string" && rec.summary.trim()
364:               ? rec.summary.trim()
365:               : "Source returned by the configured research provider.",
366:       };
367:       if (typeof rec.author === "string" && rec.author.trim()) {
368:         source.author = rec.author.trim();
369:       }
370:       if (typeof rec.publisher === "string" && rec.publisher.trim()) {
371:         source.publisher = rec.publisher.trim();
372:       }
373:       if (typeof rec.date === "string" && rec.date.trim()) {
374:         source.date = rec.date.trim();
375:       }
376:       if (typeof rec.why === "string" && rec.why.trim()) {
377:         source.why = rec.why.trim();
378:       }
379:       return source;
380:     })
381:     .filter((source): source is Source => source !== null)
382:     .slice(0, maxResults);
383: }
384: 
385: async function persist(results: Source[], query: string): Promise<void> {
386:   if (!activeFolioId) return;
387:   const all = await loadBibliography();
388:   const seen = new Set(
389:     all
390:       .filter((e) => e.folioId === activeFolioId)
391:       .map((e) => normalizeUrl(e.url)),
392:   );
393:   // Soft cap so a long session doesn't grow the bib unbounded.
394:   const existingBgForFolio = all.filter(
395:     (e) => e.folioId === activeFolioId && e.provenance === "background",
396:   ).length;
397:   let budget = Math.max(0, MAX_BACKGROUND_PER_FOLIO - existingBgForFolio);
398:   let saved = 0;
399: 
400:   for (const src of results) {
401:     if (budget <= 0) break;
402:     if (!src.url) continue;
403:     if (seen.has(normalizeUrl(src.url))) continue;
404:     if ((src.snippet?.length ?? 0) < SNIPPET_MIN_CHARS) continue;
405:     const entry: BibEntry = {
406:       id: crypto.randomUUID(),
407:       folioId: activeFolioId,
408:       title: src.title || src.url,
409:       author: src.author,
410:       publisher: src.publisher,
411:       date: src.date,
412:       url: src.url,
413:       accessedAt: Date.now(),
414:       snippet: src.snippet,
415:       why: src.why,
416:       provenance: "background",
417:       backgroundQuery: query,
418:       accepted: false,
419:     };
420:     all.push(entry);
421:     seen.add(normalizeUrl(src.url));
422:     saved += 1;
423:     budget -= 1;
424:   }
425:   if (saved > 0) {
426:     await saveBibliography(all);
427:     state.savedThisSession += saved;
428:     // Surface a passive "found N sources" event for the UI.
429:     if (typeof window !== "undefined") {
430:       window.dispatchEvent(
431:         new CustomEvent("twyne:background-sources", {
432:           detail: { saved, query, folioId: activeFolioId },
433:         }),
434:       );
435:     }
436:   }
437:   notify();
438: }

/**
 * Background agents — the Apparatus runs in the background, watching the
 * draft and surfacing sources without the writer having to ask. The model
 * is intentionally simple:
 *
 *   1. Watch the active folio for content changes (debounced, 45s).
 *   2. Derive a research query from the brief + the current draft.
 *   3. Skip the call if the same query was run recently (cache).
 *   4. Call the search provider, merge the top results into the bibliography
 *      with `provenance: "background"` so the panel can tell who found them.
 *   5. Emit `twyne:background-research` so the UI can show what is happening.
 *
 * The Convex client and a brief are required. When the client is absent
 * (offline) the watcher is a no-op — the writer will still see their
 * manually-saved sources.
 */

import type { ConvexClient } from "convex/browser";
import { api } from "../../convex/_generated/api";
import type { Source } from "../../convex/research";

1: /**
2:  * The writer's working bibliography — a flat list of sources saved from
3:  * the Apparatus panel or discovered by the research provider. Persisted
4:  * at `/bibliography.json` inside the Lix blob (per folio) so it travels
5:  * with the manuscript and syncs through the existing Convex pipeline.
6:  */
7: 
8: import { readFileAsJson, writeFileAsJson } from "./lix";
9: import type { DetectedCitation } from "../types";
10: 
11: const BIB_PATH = "/bibliography.json";
12: 
13: export type CitationStyle = "mla" | "apa" | "chicago";
14: 
15: export type BibProvenance = "writer" | "background";
16: 
17: export interface BibEntry {
18:   id: string;
19:   folioId: string;
20:   title: string;
21:   author?: string;
22:   publisher?: string;
23:   date?: string;
24:   /** Year shortcut for citation builders — mirrors the year inside `date`. */
25:   year?: string;
26:   /** DOI if the provider surfaced one. */
27:   doi?: string;
28:   url: string;
29:   accessedAt: number;
30:   /** Writer's working note — never formatted into the citation. */
31:   note?: string;
32:   /** Stable, writer-set key for in-text references (e.g. "smith2024"). */
33:   citationKey?: string;
34:   style?: CitationStyle;
35:   /** Provider-formatted citation text for `style`, when AI formatted the entry. */
36:   formattedCitation?: string;
37:   /** The display snippet, if the provider returned one. */
38:   snippet?: string;
39:   /** Why this source is relevant to the draft. */
40:   why?: string;
41:   /** Optional page hint for MLA in-text citations. */
42:   pageHint?: string;
43:   /** Who found this — the writer, or a background agent watching the draft. */
44:   provenance?: BibProvenance;
45:   /** The query a background agent was working from (when provenance = "background"). */
46:   backgroundQuery?: string;
47:   /** Whether the writer has explicitly accepted a background-saved entry. */
48:   accepted?: boolean;
49:   /** Free-form creation timestamp (used by AI-generated entries). */
50:   createdAt?: number;
51: }
52: 
53: export async function loadBibliography(): Promise<BibEntry[]> {
54:   if (typeof window === "undefined") return [];
55:   try {
56:     const data = await readFileAsJson<BibEntry[]>(BIB_PATH);
57:     return Array.isArray(data) ? data : [];
58:   } catch {
59:     return [];
60:   }
61: }
62: 
63: export async function saveBibliography(bib: BibEntry[]): Promise<void> {
64:   if (typeof window === "undefined") return;
65:   try {
66:     await writeFileAsJson(BIB_PATH, bib);
67:   } catch {
68:     // lix unavailable
69:   }
70: }
71: 
72: export async function upsertBibEntry(entry: BibEntry): Promise<BibEntry[]> {
73:   const all = await loadBibliography();
74:   const idx = all.findIndex((e) => e.id === entry.id);
75:   if (idx >= 0) all[idx] = entry;
76:   else all.push(entry);
77:   await saveBibliography(all);
78:   return all;
79: }
80: 
81: export async function deleteBibEntry(id: string): Promise<BibEntry[]> {
82:   const all = await loadBibliography();
83:   const next = all.filter((e) => e.id !== id);
84:   await saveBibliography(next);
85:   return next;
86: }

88: /* ── Citation formatters (MLA / APA / Chicago) ────────────────── */
89: 
90: function mlaEscape(s: string | undefined): string {
91:   if (!s) return "";
92:   return s.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
93: }
94: 
95: export function formatMla(e: BibEntry): string {
96:   const parts: string[] = [];
97:   const author = mlaEscape(e.author);
98:   if (author) parts.push(`${author}.`);
99:   parts.push(`"${mlaEscape(e.title)}."`);
100:   if (e.publisher) parts.push(`${mlaEscape(e.publisher)},`);
101:   if (e.date) parts.push(`${mlaEscape(e.date)},`);
102:   if (hasResolvableUrl(e.url)) {
103:     parts.push(formatUrlAccessed(e.url, e.accessedAt) + ".");
104:   }
105:   return parts.join(" ");
106: }
107: 
108: export function formatApa(e: BibEntry): string {
109:   const parts: string[] = [];
110:   const author = mlaEscape(e.author);
111:   const date = e.date ?? e.year;
112:   if (author) parts.push(`${author} (${date ?? "n.d."}).`);
113:   else if (date) parts.push(`(${date}).`);
114:   parts.push(`${mlaEscape(e.title)}.`);
115:   if (e.publisher) parts.push(`${mlaEscape(e.publisher)}.`);
116:   if (e.url) parts.push("Retrieved from " + e.url);
117:   return parts.join(" ");
118: }
119: 
120: export function formatChicago(e: BibEntry): string {
121:   const parts: string[] = [];
122:   const author = mlaEscape(e.author);
123:   if (author) parts.push(`${author}.`);
124:   parts.push(`"${mlaEscape(e.title)}."`);
125:   if (e.publisher) parts.push(`${mlaEscape(e.publisher)}.`);
126:   if (e.date ?? e.year) parts.push(`${mlaEscape(e.date ?? e.year)}.`);
127:   if (e.url) parts.push(e.url + ".");
128:   parts.push(`Accessed ${new Date(e.accessedAt).toLocaleDateString()}.`);
129:   return parts.join(" ");
130: }
131: 
132: export function formatCitation(e: BibEntry, style: CitationStyle): string {
133:   if (e.formattedCitation && e.style === style) {
134:     return e.formattedCitation;
135:   }
136:   switch (style) {
137:     case "mla":
138:       return formatMla(e);
139:     case "apa":
140:       return formatApa(e);
141:     case "chicago":
142:       return formatChicago(e);
143:   }
144: }
145: 
146: function formatUrlAccessed(url: string, ts: number): string {
147:   try {
148:     const u = new URL(url);
149:     return `${u.hostname.replace(/^www\./, "")} · accessed ${new Date(ts).toLocaleDateString()}`;
150:   } catch {
151:     return `${url} · accessed ${new Date(ts).toLocaleDateString()}`;
152:   }
153: }
154: 
155: /* ── A one-liner the writer can drop in a footnote ───────────── */
156: 
157: export function footnoteCite(e: BibEntry, style: CitationStyle): string {
158:   const author = mlaEscape(e.author) || "Anonymous";
159:   const year = e.year ?? e.date?.match(/\d{4}/)?.[0] ?? "n.d.";
160:   switch (style) {
161:     case "apa":
162:     case "chicago":
163:       return `(${author.split(",")[0]}, ${year})`;
164:     case "mla":
165:       return `(${author.split(",")[0]} ${e.pageHint ?? ""})`.trim();
166:   }
167: }
168: 
169: /* ── Dedup helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────── */
170: 
171: 
172: /** Normalize a URL for dedupe — strips trailing slashes, lowercases host. */
173: export function normalizeUrl(u: string): string {
174:   try {
175:     const x = new URL(u);
176:     return `${x.host.toLowerCase().replace(/^www\./, "")}${x.pathname}`.replace(
177:       /\/+$/,
178:       "",
179:     );
180:   } catch {
181:     return u.replace(/\/+$/, "").toLowerCase();
182:   }
183: }
184: 
185: export function hasResolvableUrl(url: string | undefined | null): boolean {
186:   return typeof url === "string" && url.trim().length > 0;
187: }
188: 
189: export async function findBibByUrl(url: string): Promise<BibEntry | undefined> {
190:   if (!hasResolvableUrl(url)) return undefined;
191:   const target = normalizeUrl(url);
192:   const all = await loadBibliography();
193:   return all.find((e) => normalizeUrl(e.url) === target);
194: }
195: 
196: export async function mergeBibEntry(entry: BibEntry): Promise<BibEntry[]> {
197:   if (!hasResolvableUrl(entry.url)) {
198:     return upsertBibEntry(entry);
199:   }
200:   const existing = await findBibByUrl(entry.url);
201:   if (existing) {
202:     return upsertBibEntry({ ...existing, ...entry, id: existing.id });
203:   }
204:   return upsertBibEntry(entry);
205: }
206: 
207: export interface FormattedCitationFields {
208:   title: string;
209:   author?: string;
210:   year?: string;
211:   date?: string;
212:   url?: string;
213:   doi?: string;
214:   publisher?: string;
215:   formatted?: string;
216:   style?: CitationStyle;
217: }
218: 
219: function stableCitationId(folioId: string, citation: DetectedCitation): string {
220:   return `ai-fmt-${folioId || "global"}-${citation.id}`.replace(
221:     /[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g,
222:     "-",
223:   );
224: }
225: 
226: export function buildBibEntryFromFormattedCitation(
227:   citation: DetectedCitation,
228:   result: FormattedCitationFields,
229:   folioId: string,
230:   now = Date.now(),
231: ): BibEntry {
232:   const date = result.date ?? result.year;
233:   return {
234:     id: stableCitationId(folioId, citation),
235:     title: result.title,
236:     author: result.author,
237:     year: result.year ?? date?.match(/\d{4}/)?.[0],
238:     date,
239:     url: result.url ?? citation.lookupUrl ?? "",
240:     doi: result.doi,
241:     publisher: result.publisher,
242:     folioId,
243:     provenance: "writer",
244:     accessedAt: now,
245:     createdAt: now,
246:     style: result.style,
247:     formattedCitation: result.formatted,
248:   };
249: }

- When the draft changes, it's debounced 45s (`onDraftChanged` from `editor/index.tsx:443` → `schedule`).
- It builds **one search query** by concatenating your brief's answers (working title + audience + goal + tone) with **the first 280 chars of the draft** (`deriveQuery`, line 89). It does not parse content — just grabs a front slice.

The user wants an agentic auto-research that:
1. Reads what they've written (the draft), autonomously identifies citable items: quotes and who said them, movies/book titles, named figures, factual claims/statistics.
2. Per item, finds a source (who said it / what movie etc.), via flexible AI-driven search.
3. Persists the findings as... "accepted-source candidates" — the bibliography (auto-biblio).
4. Keep the regex-based citation *detection* as-is.

They want "AI flexible and agentic power" instead of "hardcoded stuff". The hardcoded parts in `background-research.ts` are: `deriveQuery` (concatenating brief + 280 chars), 25-cap, snippet-length 60, "query.length < 20", etc. Those are constraints; the user mainly opposes the hardcoded heuristic query extraction and blind topical searching.

Implementation plan — build a new agentic pipeline in `background-research.ts` (or a new module) that:

**Phase 1 — Extraction (agentic, AI):**
- Feed the actual draft text (full, or chunked) + brief + already-cited citation keys/titles to the LLM.
- LLM returns a list of "citation targets": for each — the anchor text (the claim/quote/entity as it appears in the draft), a kind (quote|work|person|statistic|creative-work|direct-reference false), a reason, a suggested query, priority/importance.
- Uses the configured AI provider. New AiFeature "research-extract".
- Must be flexible: instructs the model to use its own reasoning and the tools.
- Should NOT use a web search by the model (that would be redundant/expensive); just extraction, yielding deterministic queries.
- Provide a generic LLM call that only depends on AI adapters (BYOK via `ai-client` + hosted via a new Convex action).

**Phase 2 — Lookup (agentic, flexible search):**
- For the top-K targets (by importance, bounded by e.g. 4 per pass so latency is sane), power a search. Use the model's own web-search tool when available (`research-web-search` feature), else fall back to a configured research provider (Tinyfish/MCP/Convex-hosted), which now pass the per-target query and the anchor passage.
- Reuse existing provider chain: `searchWithConfiguredProvider` from `background-research.ts` but rewritten to accept the target query. The old top-slice derivation is removed.

## Objective
- Replace Twyne's old "background research" (which blindly googled a topic query derived from the brief + first 280 chars of the draft) with a fully agentic auto-research pipeline: an AI model reads the draft, decides exactly which passages need a source (quotes, films/books, people, statistics, claims, events), returns a precise search query per item, and the background watcher resolves each claim through the configured research provider and auto-saves matched sources into the per-folio bibliography.

## Important Details

- User required: "no hardcoded stuff besides citation detection" — claim/quote/movie extraction must be AI-driven, flexible, and agentic; only the regex-based `detectCitations` in `src/utils/citations.ts:32` stays hardcoded.
- Architecture pattern follows existing BYOK client route: `resolveFeatureConfig` + `createModel` + `generateTrackedText` in `ai-client.ts`, per-feature temp/max-token defaults, feature labels in settings UI, and JSON response parsing.
- The old `convex/research.ts` provider chain (`api.research.searchSources`) remains the hosted fallback; per-apparatus-provider routing (TinyFish / model-web-search / web-mcp / hosted) mirrors the old `searchWithProvider`/`searchTinyFish`/`searchWebMcp`/`searchModelEndpoint` design.

- Support Keys must be added where typecheck demands; `convex.config.ts` deferr calmly env allowlist change avoided.

- `src/types/index.ts`: added `"research-extract"` to `AiFeature`; added `ResearchTargetKind`, `ResearchTarget`, `ResearchTargetRef` types.

/**
 * Background agents — the Apparatus runs in the background, watching the
 * draft and building an automatic bibliography without the writer having to
 * ask. The model is intentionally simple:
 *
 *   1. Watch the active folio for content changes (debounced).
 *   2. Hand the draft to the writer's AI model, which decides what genuinely
 *      needs a source: a quote to attribute, a named film or book, a
 *      statistic, a checkable claim. Each becomes a ResearchTarget carrying
 *      its own precise search query.
 *   3. Skip targets whose passage already has a saved source or was
 *      researched recently (dedupe), cap the pass at a few targets.
 *   4. Resolve each target through the configured research provider, one
 *      query at a time, and merge the best hit into the bibliography with
 *      `provenance: "background"` so the panel can tell who found them.
 *   5. Emit `twyne:background-research` and `twyne:background-sources` so
 *      the UI can show what is happening.
 *
 * The Convex client, a research provider, and an AI model are all required.
 * Missing any of those, the watcher stays a no-op — the writer still sees

parts.text:
Now I understand the current state. The user wants:

1. **More visibility in that tab (Citations panel / Apparatus) as to what claims are being researched** — a live list of targets being researched with their status (queued → searching → found/missed → saved), rather than just a status line + "last query".

2. **Results streamed** — as each target's results come in, show them incrementally (streamed into the panel), rather than only after the whole pass completes.

Currently `background-research.ts`:
- Has `lastTargetSummary` (the fresh targets) but only emitted in the snapshot's `lastTargets` after the pass starts.
- `runOnce` loops over targets sequentially: search → rank → persist. It emits events only at start (status running) and end (saved event).
- No per-target event, no "missed" case, no streaming.

Plan:
1. **Add a live activity log + target status tracking in `background-research.ts`**:
   - Maintain a `runId`/`passId` and a per-target progress map keyed by targetKey with statuses: `queued`, `searching`, `found` / `missed`, plus provider, saved count, snippet.
   - Emit a new event `twyne:background-progress` (or reuse `twyne:background-research` but include `progress` items + activity log).
   - Better: extend `snapshot()` to include:
     - `passActive: boolean`
     - `targets: ResearchProgressItem[]` (current pass live status)
     - `activity: ResearchActivity[]` (scrollback log of past claim resolutions with timestamps and outcomes)
     - Keep existing fields to avoid breaking call sites.
   - Emit `twyne:background-research` on every state change (setStatus, per-target state updates), and keep `twyne:background-sources` for the toast/bib refresh.

2. **Panel UI (citations-panel.tsx)**:
   - Render a live "researching now" list under the status line: each target shows kind badge, truncated anchor, spinner while searching, ✓ count when found, ✗ when missed.
   - Add a small "recent research" activity log (last ~6 entries: "found 1 source for 'press release …' · 08:12", "no sources for 'Deferred paragraph…'").
   - Plumb `lastTargets`/`targets`/activity into `store.research`.

3. **Apparatus page**: also show this activity (it has `showResearchLog` already but unused). Maybe expose the same upsert; keep it a shared concern. That could be a bigger job; but I can add the same rendering there cheaply.

Let me design the module change carefully.

Changes to `background-research.ts`:

```ts
export interface ResearchActivityEntry {
  id: string; // nanoid-ish
  at: number;
  kind: ResearchTargetKind; // or string
  anchor: string;
  query: string;
  outcome: "found" | "missed" | "skipped";
  count?: number;
}

export interface ResearchProgressItem {
  key: string;
  kind: string;
  anchor: string;
  query: string;
  reason?: string;
  status: "queued" | "searching" | "found" | "missed";
  savedCount: number;
  at: number;
}
```

State additions:
```ts
const progress = new Map<string, ResearchProgressItem>();
const activity: ResearchActivityEntry[] = [];
let runSequence = 0;
```

snapshot() returns extra fields:
```ts
passActive: boolean,
progress: ResearchProgressItem[],
activity: ResearchActivityEntry[],
lastTargets: ... // keep
lastSavedAt?: number
```

Events: reuse `twyne:background-research` but now fired on every mutation via a `publish()` function. Keep the event name to that both panel and apparatus re-pull; the listeners already pull the full snapshot. Fire `notify()` after every setProgress/tick.

Now in `runOnce`, after selecting `fresh`:
- Reset progress for the fresh set (or keep a session-scoped progress with all targets from the current/last pass, marked done).
- setStatus("running") then per target:
  - progress.set(key, { status:"searching" }) ; notify()
  - const res = await searchForTarget(...)
  - if (!res) → mark missed; activity.push; notify(); continue
  - find = await persistTarget(...)
  - if found>0 → mark found w/ count; activity.push; else missed; notify()

At end setStatus("idle") + notify. But `setStatus("idle")` currently also calls notify; keep.

Also stream results: after each successful `persistTarget`, we could dispatch `twyne:background-sources` per-target instead of / in addition to the aggregate at end. But the current toast says "found N sources for your draft". Streaming toasts per-claim might be nicer: emit `twyne:background-sources` with `saved: found, query, folioId, target:{kind,anchor}` etc. The panel toast shows the query + count; also refresh bib (already does). Let me emit per-claim now and remove the final aggregate event (keep it optional). Also update the toast to include the anchor/claim.

Actually to be careful about not double-personalizing, the toast handler reloads the bibliography on each event — fine.

Let me keep the final aggregate too — no, simpler: emit per-claim. But `state.savedThisSession` still aggregates. And keep final event for aggregation? The panel uses `lastBackgroundSave` toast + reload. Per-target events give more streaming "results streaming". I'll emit one `twény:background-sources` event per target pass with `{saved: found, query, folioId, anchor, kind}` and skip a stale aggregate. That gives streaming per claim.

Also I want to mark `progress` cleared after idle? Or keep the last pass's progress visible so the user sees what was researched. Better: keep the completed pass items visible (status found/missed) but mark `passActive=false`. New pass replaces the list. This gives "visibility into what claims were researched."

Now the panel changes:
- Extend `store.research` with `progress`, `activity`, `passActive`, `lastTargets` (I'll unify: `progress` replaces `lastTargets` in the store, but keep lastTargets in snapshot for compatibility since apparatus uses it? Apparatus store doesn't use lastTargets currently — it maps research lastQuery/provider only. So I can safely rename/augment).

Also, the "results streamed" aspect: the current architecture resolves each target fully before showing anything new. Streaming results means after each target's search returns, we show that claim's findings immediately (we do), and the bibliography reload shows the saved entry. That's good enough streaming at the pass level. True token streaming of a single web-search call isn't feasible (the search endpoint isn't streamed).    - Add feature label for "research-extract" — already done
3. Make errors visible with correct/retry/at-least-know options:
   - The panel currently just shows "Apparatus is offline." and a research.error string.

Let me first understand the error paths in background-research:
- `runClientResearchExtract` can throw?
- `searchForTarget` — providers return null on failure (silently swallowed). So no per-claim error info currently.
- `persistTarget` could throw.
- `runOnce` has a try/finally around the loop but no catch — exceptions propagate and reject the promise (unhandled).

So "errors visible" means: add error surfaces per-pass and per-claim:
1. Track a pass `error` when something fails (extract failure, provider errors), and display it.
2. Distinguish "searched but nothing matched" (missed, fine) from "search failed" (e.g. network error, auth failure) — show a retry affordance.
4. A "Retry" button in the panel for the last failed claim / last pass.

Let me implement:

**In background-research.ts:**
- Give `ResearchProgressItem` an `error?: string` field, so failed claims are marked as errors rather than misses. Add a status `"error"` or add `error` to status. Let me add status: `"queued" | "searching" | "found" | "missed" | "error"`.
- `searchForTarget` should return error info. Currently configured providers return null on failure (both on auth missing or fetch failing). We need to distinguish:
  - `null` = no provider configured / legitimately nothing / provider silent.
  - New: return `{ results, provider }` or throw a distinctive error.
  
Actually, let me restructure the provider search to give a richer result: `SearchResult = { ok: true, results, provider } | { ok: false, reason }`. But that's a bigger refactor of `searchWithConfiguredProvider` etc. To add error reporting with limited churn:
- Have each provider function throw `ResearchSearchError(reason)` on hard failures (fetch failed, non-ok response, missing API key?), OR return null when configuration is missing/offline intentionally.
- Then in the loop, catch: mark `row.error = reason; row.status = "error"` and log activity outcome "error", and surface it.

But I want to be careful: `searchTinyFish` returns null when `!res.ok` (e.g., 401 auth) — that's an error worth surfacing. It also returns null when key empty (config missing) — that's "no provider configured" — arguably also an error state ("Configure a key"). The fallback: if configured is null, it calls hosted `api.research.searchSources`; if that throws, it's an error.

Let me define a lightweight error channel:
```ts
interface TargetOutcome {
  results: Source[] | null;
  provider: string | null;
  error: string | null;
}
```
Modify `searchForTarget` and `searchWithConfiguredProvider` to return `outcome` with either results+provider or error string. Keep the code mostly:

```ts
async function searchForTarget(target, settings): Promise<{results, provider, error}> {
  const query = target.query;
  const context = ...;
  const configured = await searchWithConfiguredProvider(query, context, settings);
  if (configured.error) return configured;
  if (configured.results?.length) return configured;
  // configured came back with no results (provider worked, empty) → fall to hosted
  if (configured.provider) return configured; // provider worked but no hits — что means missed, not error
  // configured is null (provider unset/not configurable) → hosted
  ...
}
```

Hmm, this is getting complicated. Let me simplify semantics:

`searchWithConfiguredProvider` returns:
- `{ results: Source[], provider: string }` — success (possibly empty results).
- `null` — either provider not configured or threw. 

We need to distinguish "provider not configured" from "provider tried and erred". For UX:
- `settings.researchProvider` tells us which provider is configured. If the provider is "tinyfish" but no key → "Add a TinyFish key in Settings". If key present but API 401 → "TinyFish returned an error". If provider is web-mcp but no endpoint → "Set an MCP endpoint". Etc.

```
